names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 13 Απριλίου, «Άγιος Αρσένιος Αρχιεπίσκοπος Ελασσώνος», with the rank word and the see left off.

birth.note: saint.gr: «Ο Άγιος Αρσένιος γεννήθηκε στην Ευρυτανία, το έτος 1548 μ.Χ., από γονείς ευσεβείς και φιλόθεους, τον Θεόδωρο και την Χριστοδούλη», and the page's heading has «(1548 - 1625)».

death.note: saint.gr: «αλλά έμεινε οριστικά στη Ρωσία, όπου και κοιμήθηκε με ειρήνη το έτος 1625 μ.Χ.», and the page's heading has «(1548 - 1625)».

attestations.note: CHECKED ON 13 OCTOBER 2026, AND STILL NO ROW — the one fetch a previous reader named as decisive was made and it came back negative. The line that raised the question is on the Julian 4 августа: «Обретение мощей свт. Арсения Элассонского.», with no year, behind an icon captioned «Свт. Арсений еп. Элассонский» and a name link to page 14955. The man is not in doubt — this corpus's Arsenius is the archbishop who stayed in Russia, was administrator of the province of Suzdal and was buried in the metropolitan church there, which is where a finding of his relics would be. What was in doubt was whether that line is a SECOND day for a man this calendar already keeps on his own day, which is the only footing on which the row was to be made. It is not. **The day page for 13 апреля ст. ст., days.pravoslavie.ru/Days/20260413.html, was fetched and holds no Арсений of any kind** — not him, not any of the corpus's nine other Arseniuses. And name page 14955 heads «Святитель Арсений Элассонский / День памяти: 4 августа» — one day, and it is the finding of the relics. So this calendar keeps no commemoration of Arsenius himself at all, only the finding; «Обретение мощей» is a feast and not a folder or a commemoration of the saint's own day (BRIEF-RUSSIAN §6), and there is no day of his own here for it to be a second of. The row stays undocumented and the reading is written here so that the next reader does not spend the fetch again. NOT CHECKED: whether any other Russian source keeps him on 13 апреля; the year of the обретение, which the line does not give; whether the Greek 13 Απριλίου is itself a translation feast rather than a repose, saint.gr giving only «κοιμήθηκε με ειρήνη το έτος 1625» and no day for the death.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (30 September 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 13ης Απριλίου — «Άγιος Αρσένιος Αρχιεπίσκοπος Ελασσώνος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 13 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and heads him «(1548 - 1625)». The day's line and its own verses call him Αρχιεπίσκοπος, while the page's prose has him elected Επίσκοπος «Δημονίκου και Ελασσώνος» in 1574; the office here follows the day's line and the title he gave himself, and the prose's form is in the life. It says plainly of one thing that it does not know it: «Που έμαθε τα γράμματα δεν μας είναι γνωστό», where he learnt his letters is not known to us. The picture captions put his body in a shrine inside the metropolitan church of Suzdal in Russia, where it had been buried. He is none of the nine other Arseniuses in the corpus.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue on pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (30 September 2026).

hymns.text: Ελασσώνος ποιμένα Θετταλίας το κλέισμα και της Μοσχοβίας απάσης περιβόητον άκουσμα. Αρσένιον υμνήσωμεν πιστοί, βοώντες μετά πόθου ευλαβώς· φύλαττε και σκέπε πάτερ αεί τους πίστει σοι κραυγάζοντας· δόξα τω σε δοξάσαντι Χριστό, δόξα τω σε θαυμαστώσαντι, δόξα τω δωρουμένω δια σου χάριν και έλεος.

source.text: saint.gr — Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος α', Τῆς ἐρήμου πολίτης, on the page of Άγιος Αρσένιος Αρχιεπίσκοπος Ελασσώνος. It is his own and names him, his see and Muscovy; the page prints it in monotonic spelling, as it stands here.

english.text: The shepherd of Elassona, the glory of Thessaly and the far-renowned report of all Muscovy — Arsenius let us the faithful hymn, crying to him with longing and reverence: guard and shelter always, O father, those who cry to thee in faith. Glory to Christ who glorified thee, glory to him who made thee wonderful, glory to him who gives grace and mercy through thee.
